name: Fix the Bug
description: A coding-agent test. The model is dropped into a small real JavaScript repository with a README, a failing visible test suite and two or three planted bugs (rounding, off-by-one, shared mutable state, date logic, async ordering, a lost `this`). Using one text action per turn (LIST, READ, SEARCH, WRITE, PATCH, RUN_TESTS, SUBMIT) it must investigate, edit files and make the tests pass within 30 actions and 150,000 output tokens. The tests are read-only and everything runs in the sandbox on an in-memory copy of the repo. After SUBMIT, hidden tests that check the same behaviour more thoroughly decide the score, so hard-coding the visible tests does not work. Four repos: an invoice calculator, a text-adventure parser, a date library and an LRU cache with an API client.
hook: A real repo, a red test suite and 30 actions. Can it find the bugs — and do the hidden tests agree?
author: Gauntlet Core
